{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment is negative or shows early signs of bearishness (e.g., sentiment < 0.33).",
    "Increase forecast sensitivity to recent price spikes — if last 3-5 days show upward momentum, apply a 10-15% upward bias to prevent undershooting.",
    "Apply mean reversion correction: if forecast is significantly below 30-day moving average, adjust upward by 2-5% to align with historical trend.",
    "Reduce forecast volatility during low-sentiment periods — avoid overreacting to short-term noise when sentiment is flat or negative.",
    "When sentiment is positive and price is rising, apply a slight lag correction — forecast should be 1-2 days behind actual trend to avoid over-optimism.",
    "For high-sentiment periods with strong upward momentum, add a 5-10% buffer to forecast to account for potential overshoots.",
    "If true outcome consistently exceeds forecast by >5% over 3-5 days, consider increasing forecast baseline by 2-3% to account for lagged market reaction."
  ]
}
